item.description:
New research on anonymous credentials explores dynamic multi-authority updates to enhance privacy. For identity pros, it promises more robust, privacy-preserving authentication options. However, practical application in decentralized systems remains limited by framework complexity.
— via arXiv

item.title: Beyond SSO and MFA: Why your identity security strategy needs continuous control
item.description:
Okta outlines why identity security must evolve beyond SSO and MFA to include continuous control. For identity leaders, this approach is crucial for real-time threat detection. The downside: continuous control requires investment in advanced monitoring infrastructure.
— via Okta

item.title: NIST and CISA finalize playbook to stop token theft and forgery
item.description:
NIST and CISA have finalized a playbook to combat token theft and forgery for federal agencies and cloud providers. It gives detailed steps to bolster key management and token verification processes. This guidance is targeted and won't strengthen non-federal or unsupported setups.
— via Help Net Security

item.title: Proof’s VDC launch brings together banking regulation, reusable identity and AI agents
item.description:
Proof launched a Verifiable Digital Credential (VDC) system for cross-platform identity reuse. It lets users verify once and use their creds across banks and more, aligning with new U.S. regulatory guidance. Adoption heavily hinges on which institutions accept Proof's credentials.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Active Exploitation Attempts Target WSO2 API Manager JWT Bypass With Forged Admin Tokens
item.description:
A security flaw in WSO2 API Manager is under active exploitation. Attackers could bypass JWT checks to hijack accounts due to a signature-verification slip. Patching may disrupt integrations or custom JWT logic, needing careful testing.
— via The Hacker News

item.title: Deal for cybersecurity lab expands Fime’s digital identity assurance portfolio
item.description:
Fime grows its portfolio with a cybersecurity lab acquisition. They've boosted their capabilities in digital trust and compliance testing. This move is primarily relevant to organizations needing certified alignment with biometric and digital ID standards.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: OSD granted patent for biometric barcode security and authentication
item.description:
OSD's new patent covers a biometric barcode for identity document security. It promises more secure data on physical IDs using a mix of biometrics and open ledger tech. It's early days, so widespread implementation isn't immediate.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Building sustainable identity governance in complex cloud environments
item.description:
Injecting identity governance into cloud operations is the focus here. The discussion is about marrying identity management with broader governance in complex environments. This isn't a step-by-step guide—it's conceptual insights, needing adaptation to actual conditions.
— via Identity Week

item.title: A new way to sign into One Login using passkeys
item.description:
Passkeys come to One Login on GOV.UK. It's part of ongoing trials to enhance the user onboarding experience. Full rollout requires user education and feedback refinement.
— via Identity Week

item.title: eBook: Identity-First Threat Intelligence
item.description:
An eBook discusses identity-first threat intelligence. It highlights how stolen credentials are a growing threat and where traditional defenses fail. The advice is general and lacks immediate prescriptive actions.
— via Help Net Security

item.title: KREMLIN Banking Malware Hijacks Chrome and Edge to Steal Credentials and Session Tokens
item.description:
New malware, KREMLIN, targets Brazilian bank credentials via browser hijacking. It highlights the need for vigilant browser extension security policies. Currently, it impacts specific browsers and locales, but watch for wider spreads.
— via The Hacker News

item.title: Biometric Update: Singapore expands Singpass passkeys to Android users
item.description:
Singapore's Singpass system rolls out Android passkey logins. It broadens access to a password-free, secure authentication method for many users. But, it'll take time to see complete adoption since it's being pushed out gradually via updates.
— via FIDO Alliance

item.title: Plug 'n' Pray: Agentic LLM-based Detection of Potential Log File Exposures in Third-Party Content Management System Plugins
item.description:
A paper proposes an AI framework for identifying exposed CMS log files. It aims to prevent data leaks through unsecured plugin logs. But practical application depends on integration capability with existing CMS setups.
— via arXiv

item.title: AI is exposing a security structure built for yesterday’s threats
item.description:
A post highlights how outdated security models fail against AI-driven threats. It underlines the need to adapt strategies to AI-enhanced impersonation and social engineering. Realignment efforts will need to cross traditional security silos.
— via CSO Online

item.title: How Humans and LLMs Read Gender into Gender-Neutral Physical Descriptions
item.description:
Research highlights gender bias in 'neutral' descriptions by AI models. This impacts how identity and characteristics are communicated in digital spaces. It's an alert on the nuances in deploying AI to infer identities without bias.
— via arXiv

item.title: Who gets to define an AI agent's intent?
item.description:
A post from WorkOS discusses defining AI agent intent and resource access management. It's about maintaining security in automated environments. Execution varies by organizational policy compliance needs.
— via WorkOS

item.title: Product showcase: mSecure makes one vault do more than remember passwords
item.description:
mSecure is enhancing its password manager to handle more than just passwords. It integrates multiple devices with AES-256 encryption, offering a single vault for sensitive information. This enhances data protection and convenience for users, but limits apply if you're not using iOS, Android, macOS, or Windows.
— via Help Net Security

item.title: Interoperability, adoption now critical questions facing UK digital identity effort
item.description:
Interoperability and adoption hurdles are significant for the UK's digital identity initiatives. Addressing these challenges is vital for widespread acceptance and effectiveness of digital IDs. However, progress is slowed by fragmented systems and varying regional regulations.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Cyprus opens bidding for €9.8M digital ID upgrade, EUDI Wallet integration contract
item.description:
Cyprus is upgrading its digital services and integrating with the EU's Digital Identity Wallet. This contract aims to enhance citizen services and secure digital identity management. The project faces potential delays due to the complexity of integration and technology updates required.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Germany unveils national EUDI wallet ‘d-you’
item.description:
Germany has revealed its national EUDI wallet, 'd-you', for storing digital IDs on smartphones. This wallet is slated to advance digital self-determination for citizens. Yet, the January 2027 launch means users must wait for these benefits, and adoption rates are uncertain.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Twitch extension with 30K installs exposes users’ OAuth tokens
item.description:
A Twitch extension with 30,000 installs exposed users' OAuth session tokens. This vulnerability poses significant risks for unauthorized access to Twitch accounts. The core issue: many users remain unaware their tokens are compromised until it's too late.
— via BleepingComputer

item.title: Passkey enrolment pretext leads to a spike in Microsoft social engineering attacks
item.description:
Passkey enrolment social engineering attacks are increasing, targeting Microsoft users. This technique manipulates passkey setups to compromise cloud identities. The flaw here is in traditional user education, which often overlooks this passkey manipulation vector.
— via Identity Week

item.title: Webinar: How malicious OAuth apps can lead to Google Workspace breaches
item.description:
A webinar highlights the risks of malicious OAuth apps leading to Google Workspace breaches. This showcases vulnerabilities through social engineering and OAuth exploitation. Awareness alone isn’t enough due to the sophisticated tactics used in these attacks.
— via BleepingComputer

item.title: 3BB Attacker Used MeshCentral Backdoor for Root Access, Targeted Subscriber Credentials
item.description:
3BB's network was infiltrated using MeshCentral, compromising subscriber credentials. This incident shows how legitimate tools can become significant insider threats. The exploitation's detection relied heavily on luck and post-event analysis.
— via The Hacker News

item.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit Chrome-Windows Zero-Day Chain to Deploy GRIMWEDGE
item.description:
China-linked hackers are exploiting a Chrome-Windows zero-day chain to deliver a backdoor called GRIMWEDGE. This presents a direct threat through spear-phishing campaigns targeting NGOs, bypassing patched vulnerabilities. The catch: only those on the latest browser versions are protected.
— via The Hacker News

item.title: A maximum severity GitLab flaw could turn your CI/CD server into an attacker’s treasure trove
item.description:
A critical flaw in GitLab could allow attackers to access arbitrary files and sensitive data. This vulnerability, marked at maximum severity, can expose credentials on CI/CD servers. The limitation is that exploitation is conditional, requiring specific misconfigurations.
— via CSO Online

item.title: Cybersecurity jobs available right now: September 15, 2026
item.description:
Job openings in cybersecurity reflect growing demands in credential management and security architecture. This move highlights the expanding role of AI and security integration in maintaining secure environments. Geographical and skill limitations might restrict applicants.
— via Help Net Security

item.title: Japan's Digital Agency says VPN flaw exposed 246,000 personnel records
item.description:
A VPN flaw exposed 246,000 personnel records in Japan, highlighting the risks of vulnerable remote access solutions. Such exposure can lead to significant personal and organizational damage. Mitigating the issue depends heavily on timely patch deployments.
— via BleepingComputer

item.title: UK.gov begins killing off passwords for 23 million users
item.description:
The UK government is transitioning 23 million users away from passwords to passkeys. This shift aims to reduce phishing attempts and improve user security. The journey is phased, and challenges remain in account recovery and user adaptability.
— via The Register Security

item.title: Why Identity Security Requires Continuous Resilience and Why Our Investment Here Matters
item.description:
Continuous resilience in identity security involves regular updates beyond initial verification, crucial for maintaining trust. Jumio's emphasis on sustained checks highlights ongoing risks in static identity management. The key challenge is adjusting policies to accommodate this dynamic approach.
— via Jumio

item.title: What we know about the Revolut data breach so far
item.description:
Hackers accessed Revolut's customer data by pretending to be from a government agency. This breach sheds light on the need for stringent verification of requests, especially those appearing official. The tricky part is balancing thorough scrutiny with operational efficiency.
— via Help Net Security

item.title: Permify: Open-source authorization as a service
item.description:
Permify, an open-source tool, simplifies runtime authorization outside app code. This can make managing complex permissions easier and less prone to coding errors. However, teams need to integrate it with existing infrastructure, which could mean upfront work.
— via Help Net Security

item.title: Attackers Use Passkey Phishing to Hijack Microsoft Cloud Accounts and Exfiltrate Data
item.description:
Microsoft reports phishing using passkey themes to breach cloud accounts. It's a reminder that even advanced security measures aren't immune to social engineering. But the approach relies on user interaction, still making user education a critical line of defense.
— via The Hacker News

item.title: Revolut confirms customer data breach through fake government requests
item.description:
Revolut suffered a data breach because attackers faked government requests. This incident highlights the threat of social engineering that exploits trust-based processes. The catch is the challenge of verifying every government request without slowing operations.
— via Hacker News

item.title: Week in review: Linux rootkit deployed on F5 BIG-IP APM devices, Cisco FMC bugs exploited
item.description:
Recent headlines cover rootkits on F5 devices and exploited Cisco bugs. For zero-trust models, it underscores the concept that perimeter defenses are never enough. The limitation is that many existing systems aren’t zero-trust ready and need upgrades.
— via Help Net Security

item.title: Accredited testing lab options grow as IAD providers seek edge in burgeoning market
item.description:
More labs are now available to verify the efficacy of biometric injection attack detection. This helps businesses pick reliable solutions amid rising bypass tactics. However, lab testing adds another step and cost to already stretched budgets.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: DHS launches $440M government-wide biometric capture procurement
item.description:
The DHS seeks standardized biometric capture devices across US federal agencies. It aims to unify capabilities and reduce varied device use, easing interoperability. The challenge lies in transitioning legacy systems without disrupting services.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Securing AI Agent Tool Calls in Azure: Identity, Authorization, and Verified Execution
item.description:
Azure's new features aim to secure AI tools with solid identity verification. This could enhance trust in AI interactions by controlling access securely. The downside is it requires organizations already invested in Azure ecosystems to apply effectively.
— via Microsoft Entra

item.title: ThreatsDay: 200 Android Flaws, Browser-Built Phishing, 119K Scam Shops + 23 More Stories
item.description:
The recent spree of flaws exposes persistent issues like outdated permissions. Each incident points to overlooked basics like permissions, even within secure domains. Addressing these basics requires consistent audits, not yet a universal practice.
— via The Hacker News

item.title: Protecting organizations from AI-assisted executive impersonation and invoice fraud
item.description:
Microsoft spots AI-aided scams that use fake exec emails for invoice fraud. This evolution in BEC tactics stresses safeguarding email identities further. Unfortunately, distinguishing real from fake AI-generated content remains a hurdle with current tools.
— via Microsoft Security

item.title: Detect and disrupt AI-themed attacks with Microsoft Defender
item.description:
Microsoft Defender introduces tools targeting AI-themed attacks. This effort helps identify and stop threats leveraging machine learning aspects early. Yet, it’s solely effective within Defender's ecosystem, which means limited cross-tool compatibility.
— via Microsoft Security

item.title: Stealth rootkit targeting F5 BIG-IP could expose enterprise identity gateways
item.description:
A stealth rootkit for F5 BIG-IP puts enterprise identity gateways at risk. It's a wake-up call to monitor these critical systems constantly for compromised components. The catch is that many organizations overlook these less-visible attack surfaces.
— via CSO Online

item.title: CISA Flags Exploited Cisco, Citrix, Fortinet Flaws, Sets Sept. 12 Federal Patch Deadline
item.description:
CISA highlights urgent patches for Cisco and others, flagging potential exploits. It’s a clear push to reduce attack surfaces by urging swift patch application. Widespread patching, however, requires downtime planning, often leading to organizational delays.
— via The Hacker News

item.title: MikroTik patches flaws currently being exploited to take over routers
item.description:
MikroTik fixed exploitable flaws in their router OS, currently under attack in the wild. Addressing these issues promptly is vital to prevent unauthorized control over devices. Still, not all users promptly apply updates, leaving many systems vulnerable.
— via CSO Online

item.title: Digital sovereignty, infrastructure and credential formats colliding
item.description:
Credential formats are facing new pressures amid debates on digital sovereignty. Moving from physical ID documents to digital credentials is a growing trend. The challenge: transitioning without a solid cryptographic foundation is risky and complex.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Revolut confirms customer data breach, falling for fake government requests
item.description:
Revolut fell victim to a data breach from fake government requests for customer data. This underscores the vulnerability of relying on official-looking requests without proper verification. The catch: it shows how social engineering can bypass even sophisticated security measures.
— via Hacker News

item.title: CISA Adds 5 Actively Exploited Artifactory, ScreenConnect, and RouterOS Flaws to KEV
item.description:
CISA identified five new vulnerabilities in widely used systems like JFrog Artifactory. These flaws are actively exploited, requiring urgent patching. But the issue is many organizations may not yet have detected their exposure to these vulnerabilities.
— via The Hacker News

item.title: Public sector joins digital identity export market as countries package DPI capacity
item.description:
Public sectors worldwide are packaging their digital identity solutions for export. This promotes international collaboration on digital identity systems. The hurdle: adapting solutions to differing legal and technical standards globally.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Attackers use passkey-themed scams to hijack Microsoft 365 accounts
item.description:
Scammers use passkey-themed lures to target Microsoft 365 users. These scams effectively deceive employees by impersonating IT personnel to gain account access. The limitation: even with better training, human error remains hard to totally eliminate.
— via CSO Online

item.title: Ant International, Visa, Mastercard work to make agentic protocols interoperable
item.description:
Visa, Mastercard, and Ant International aim for interoperability in agentic protocols. This could streamline onboarding for digital wallets and payments. The barrier: integrating these protocols across different ecosystems without disruption can be complex.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Digital ID policy was scrapped, but government’s access challenges remain
item.description:
Despite scrapping a digital ID policy, the UK government still faces access hurdles. This affects the modernization of public service access. The roadblock: inconsistent approaches and changing policies hinder progress.
— via Identity Week

item.title: SpyCloud 2026 Identity Threat Report Finds Non-Human Identities Are Now the Leading Path into the Enterprise
item.description:
Non-human identities are now a major route for breaches into enterprises. This finding from SpyCloud's report highlights overlooked AI and machine identity risks. The downside: most organizations overestimate their monitoring capabilities in this area.
— via CSO Online

item.title: Your Critical Vulnerabilities Might Not Be Your Biggest Risk
item.description:
A post argues that critical vulnerabilities might not always pose the biggest risks. It suggests focusing on vulnerabilities with real pathways to compromise. The challenge: prioritizing effectively without under-placing serious vulnerabilities.
— via The Hacker News

item.title: AI agents exploited PaperCut flaws to breach 395 organizations
item.description:
AI agents played a pivotal role in exploiting PaperCut software flaws across organizations. The automated process significantly breaches security perimeters efficiently. Mitigation is difficult as AI-driven attacks evolve faster than detection tools.
— via Help Net Security
